title: wOS app manifest (wos-app.json)
description: What a wOS app is and what turning it on installs: its tools, tables, server part and screens. See packages/manifest/README.md.

id.description: Lower-case id. It is also the tool and event namespace (chat.post_message, chat.message.posted) and the table prefix (chat_messages).

name.description: What people see in the left rail, sentence case.

description.description: One plain sentence: what the app does.

version.description: Semantic version of the app package.

license.description: SPDX id. The suite is AGPL-3.0-only; apps should be AGPL- or Apache-compatible.

core.description: Semver range of the suite core, for example >=0.1.

apps.description: Other apps this one needs ON (rare: prefer events and tools that degrade when absent). Map of app id to semver range.

tables.description: Path to the migrations folder: NNNN_name.sql files, applied in order when the app is turned on and on every start. See README.

server.description: Path to the server part: an ES module whose default export is register(ctx) returning { handlers, routes?, start?, stop? }.

screens.description: Path to the screen part: an ES module whose default export is { mount(el, ctx) }. Downloaded by the browser only when the app is on.

icon.description: Icon name from the kit's icon set, or a path to a 24x24 SVG.

order.description: Position in the left rail, low first. Core apps use 0 to 19.

hidden.description: No left rail entry (an app that only adds tools).

listens.description: Events from other apps this app reacts to. Missing apps simply never send them.

services.description: Extra services a self-hoster must run, by docker compose profile name, for example livekit.

permissions.description: Browser or OS permissions the screens ask for: notifications, camera, microphone, screen.

desktop.description: Desktop-only capabilities: spawn, terminal, keychain, global_shortcut.

env.description: Environment variables the server part reads. Name them in plain words in the README.

onDisable.description: keep: tables and files stay when the app is turned off (the default). Data is only deleted by apps.uninstall, which exports first.

exports.description: What the app's export contains, by plain name.

core.description: Part of the suite core and cannot be turned off (Agents, Settings). Apps from other repos never set this.

mount.description: For apps whose existing server-rendered pages the suite shows in a frame until native screens exist (the CRM and the board today).

path.description: Where the suite serves the app's own pages, for example /m/crm.

start.description: First page inside the frame, relative to path.
